newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish share prices slip a little, eyes on Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Irish share prices slip a little, eyes on Wall St.

text.p: Leading Irish share prices were marked down in morning trade on Tuesday but dealers said the response to last night's sharp drop in Wall Street had been reasonably muted.

Investors are now awaiting the U.S. open to see how the Dow fares today after it tumbled by 192 points yesterday, the second-largest single-day point drop in its history after the Black Monday market crash of 1987.
"Right across Europe, equity markets have reacted calmly. Prices are a touch easier in Dublin but so far the market hasn't show a huge negative reaction," one trader said.
"People are holding back to see what happens," he added.
By 0932 GMT, the ISEQ index of Irish shares was down 10.83 points or 0.32 percent at 3,346.01.
Among financial stocks, Bank of Ireland lost three pence to 715, Allied Irish Banks shed two pence to 510 while Irish Life and Irish Permanent lost three pence to 337 and 607 respectively.
Industrials also weakened with Elan, which is mainly traded in New York, losing 69 pence to 2836, which dragged the overall index downward.
Smurfit was down three pence at 190 and Kerry Group shed 10 pence to 630.
One of the few stocks to buck the general trend was agricultural wholesaler IAWS, which was reported to be in talks to rescue the troubled Bell Lines shipping group.
